newsitem.title: UK: Rainfall still hampers European beet crop - Licht.
newsitem.headline: Rainfall still hampers European beet crop - Licht.

text.p: Wet weather across western Europe's beet growing areas is continuing to hamper the late harvest but delays to final processing are likely to be minimal, statistician F.O. Licht said on Wednesday.
"The wet weather continues to stall the late harvest but declines have been minor since much of the crop has been harvested," Licht said in its daily report.
Additional rainfall expected this week would continue to slow the harvest, it said.
Levels of precipitation across the United Kingdom, for example, reached 12 to 15 mm in the week ended November 26.
The United Kingdom, which has an extended beet campaign, is where the bulk of the region's unharvested beet crops remain.
Scattered rainfall amounting to 6 to 18 mm was seen during the period in eastern Europe where the harvest is essentially completed, Licht said.
"In the former Soviet Union, favourably dry weather conditions during the past month of the harvest led to a slight improvement in crop production," the report said.
But output would still be lower than last year, it said.
